quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so others know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know your plans in advance.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until the light changes to green or a green arrow appears before you go. Unless a sign says otherwise, do not proceed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The bridge ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge ahead has low clearance. Do not go under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: Must you signal every time you pull away from a curb?
questions.explanation: You must use your turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: What should you do before starting your engine?

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only adults have their seat belts on.
Make sure only children have their seat belts on.
Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your own seat belt. Make sure every person in the car does the same.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When driving near children, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run into the street without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and could run into the street suddenly without looking.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive the same as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the space between you and the car ahead. Your vehicle will take longer to stop.

questions.question: When passing a car that just parked on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Expect the driver to open the door as you approach.
Expect the driver to wait until you pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the door as you approach.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. The driver may open the door suddenly as you pass. Use extra caution near parked vehicles.

questions.question: When driving uphill behind a heavy truck, what should you know?

options.text: The truck may go slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slowly on hills, especially slower than the speed limit. You may not be able to pass safely. On hills with poor visibility, passing is illegal. Be careful when approaching trucks from behind.

questions.question: It is illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full traffic lane. Two motorcycles may share a lane, but cars cannot share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with a flashing signal, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for warning signs like lowered gates or train sounds.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, nighttime driving is:
questions.explanation: Nighttime driving is more dangerous than daytime driving. Visibility is lower, glare from other headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a sharp right turn ahead.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually white with black markings. They control traffic movement and must always be obeyed.

questions.question: You can avoid alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding before drinking that you will not drive.
Saying "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving crashes is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe decisions later.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you must:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Only go when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is approaching. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes, reducing visibility.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive above 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on low beam headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. High beams reflect off fog and rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your crash risk.
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving is a distraction that increases your crash risk.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Brake hard to make the other driver back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times a minute to see if a car is following too closely or trying to pass. If a car is tailgating you, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when vehicles follow too closely.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gas?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Every quick stop wastes fuel because you have to speed up again to match traffic. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When you enter a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means what color light will come next?
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light will come next soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They tell you about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you that a lane is ending. Get ready to let traffic merge safely.
